samples.summary: The housekeeping store's `userId` is recorded by the test harness and never asserted — nothing pins the scope that archive recovery reads under
samples.evidence: `offline-runtime.test.tsx:32` declares `const constructed: Array<{ userId: string }> = []`, line 37 pushes the constructor options into it, and line 96 clears it in `beforeEach` — but no `expect` in the file ever reads `constructed` (grep for `constructed` in that file returns only lines 32, 37 and 96). The `WafflebaseDocStore` this runtime builds is what `listRecoverableWork` and `recoverOfflineCopy` run against, and `WafflebaseDocStore.listArchives()`/`loadArchive()` scope purely on that `userId`. If `OfflineRuntime` constructed it with the wrong identity (or a stale one after the `userId` prop changed), the session would be offered another account's archived documents back and could materialise them as new documents it owns — exactly the cross-account leak `wafflebase-doc-store-archive.test.ts` is careful about at the store layer. The harness already captures the value; one `expect(constructed[0]).toEqual({ userId: '42', isOpenElsewhere: expect.any(Function) })` would close it.
searchedFor: checked src/components/__tests__/private-route.test.tsx (asserts only the prop passed to a mocked OfflineRuntime)

samples.summary: The reconcile's `isOpenElsewhere` is asserted only to be a function, not to carry the `userId`/`whenUnknown: false` scoping the code calls load-bearing
samples.evidence: The case "tells the reconcile what it may not judge on an absence" ends with `expect(typeof options.isOpenElsewhere).toBe('function')` (line 168) — true for any function whatsoever. `offline-runtime.tsx` builds it as `isOpenInAnyTab(docKey, { userId, whenUnknown: false })`, and its own comment says both terms matter: an unscoped question lets another account's open document defer this account's cleanup, and `whenUnknown: true` would switch the sweep off in a browser that cannot answer. `durable-session.test.ts` proves `isOpenInAnyTab` honours those options, but nothing proves the runtime passes them. `durable-session` is not mocked in this suite, so a `vi.spyOn` plus one invocation of the captured callback would assert it.
searchedFor: read src/lib/durable-session.test.ts 'seeing what other tabs hold'

samples.summary: No test covers which lapse `CollabDocumentProvider` publishes, so the design's "the tooltip must name which case applies" is unverified for every call-site cause
samples.evidence: `collab-document-provider.tsx:291` derives `unsupported` / `not-permitted` / `not-enabled` / `another-tab` from four separate conditions. Grepping `another-tab|not-enabled|unsupported|not-permitted` under `src/components/__tests__` returns nothing, and `lapse|DurabilityLapse` appears in no `.test.tsx` under `src/`. The only coverage is `sync-status-chip.test.tsx`, which either calls `tooltipFor(...)` with a lapse handed to it (line 637) or mounts `DurabilityLapseScope` by hand (`strandedUnderScopes`). So the mapping from "lost the election" to `'another-tab'` — the one diagnosis a user can act on — could be inverted or omitted with the whole suite green, which is precisely the failure the diff's own comment on the nesting order says it is guarding against.

samples.summary: Three new tooltip branches are unexercised: the `saved-locally` sentence, the connected/disconnected split in `not-saved`, and the `offerOffline` sentence
samples.evidence: `tooltipFor` is called in tests only at `sync-status-chip.test.tsx:637` (`tooltipFor('not-saved', null, false, false, lapse)`) and :689 (`'saved'`). So: (a) the `saved-locally` case at sync-status-tooltip.ts:57 — the one state this feature adds — has no assertion on its text anywhere (grep `will be sent when syncing` matches only the source); (b) `connected` is always `false`, so the new "rejected by the server" wording is never produced; (c) `offerOffline` is always `false`, so the ' Click to save documents you open later on this device. These changes stay in this tab.' sentence is never asserted — notably, the analogous "must not promise to save *these* edits" property *is* tested for the toast action label but not for this sentence, which is the one a user reads before deciding whether a reload is safe.
searchedFor: grep `saved-locally|will be sent when syncing` across packages/frontend

samples.summary: The traversal test's positive assertion is weakened from every request to some request, so a regression that drops the encoded id from the named route can now pass
samples.evidence: The loop previously asserted `expect(pathname).toContain(encodeURIComponent(TRAVERSAL))` for every URL; it now asserts only `paths.some(...)` (lines 170-174). For `deleteWorkspace`, `documentIdsIn` issues a `fetchWorkspace(TRAVERSAL)` that already contains the encoded id, so the `some` predicate is satisfied by the *companion* request — the DELETE the case is named for is no longer required to carry the id at all. The remaining per-URL guard only rejects the literal normalized `/auth/logout`, which this specific payload happens to produce; an id interpolated raw at a different nesting depth, or a route that stopped carrying the id, would now slip through. A stronger fix would be to exempt only argument-free companion calls (e.g. assert every URL that is not `.../documents` carries the encoded id).

samples.summary: The `keepArchives` option on `dropAllForUser`/`eraseOfflineData` has no caller and no test, so its documented "expired session keeps archives" behaviour is unverified and unreachable
samples.evidence: `grep keepArchives` across packages/frontend matches only the two declarations (`wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1085,1123` and `offline-erase.ts:29`) — no call site ever passes it, and no case in `offline-erase.test.ts` or `wafflebase-doc-store-archive.test.ts` sets it. Every erase test asserts archives *are* dropped, so the `keepArchives: true` branch at wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1123 is dead in both senses. The 401 path the comment cites now erases nothing at all (`eraseLocalData: "none"`), so if that policy ever changes back, the branch it would rely on has never been executed.

samples.summary: `dropArchivesWhere`'s `onlyUser` narrowing is never passed by any caller and never tested
samples.evidence: `grep onlyUser` across src matches only the parameter declaration and its body (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1300-1322). Both call sites — `dropArchivesWhere(BY_USER, IDBKeyRange.only(userId))` in `dropAllForUser` and `dropArchivesWhere(BY_ARCHIVED_AT, range)` in `collectStale` — omit it, so the intersection logic (including the `theirs.has(id)` filter) is executed by no test in `wafflebase-doc-store-archive.test.ts` or `-cleanup.test.ts`. Dead branches in a deletion path are the ones worth either exercising or removing.

samples.summary: `belongsToAnotherUser`'s skip branch is untested — only the "key names nobody" fallback is exercised, so an over-matching regex would silently stop collecting this user's orphans
samples.evidence: The only orphan-snapshot case is `wafflebase-doc-store-atomicity.test.ts` "an entry that predates the header rule is collected rather than living forever out of reach", which seeds the key `doc-a`; that key matches no `wb:` segment, so `belongsToAnotherUser` returns `false` on the default path. No test seeds an orphan under `pk/wb:{secret}:{otherUser}:sheet-x` to prove it is skipped, and none seeds one under this user's own `wb:` key to prove it is still collected. The regex at line 1273 is the only attribution an orphan has; if it matched the current user's keys too, orphan collection would silently stop and the leak this method exists to close would persist with the suite green.
searchedFor: read wafflebase-doc-store-atomicity.test.ts 'an entry that predates the header rule'

samples.summary: `touch()` — the on-load `updatedAt` write added so other tabs can see an open-but-unedited document — has no test
samples.evidence: `load()` now fires `void this.touch(docKey)` to record the read in the database, with a comment that without it "a document opened and never written would stay the oldest row in every other tab's view". No test reads through one store instance and then checks that a *second* instance's `collectStale`/eviction spares it: `wafflebase-doc-store-cleanup.test.ts` covers the same-instance case via the `touched` set ("never evicts a document this session has open") and the cross-instance case via the injected `isOpenElsewhere` double, never via the persisted timestamp. Failure is contained — `isOpenElsewhere` is the primary guard — but the fallback this method is for is unverified.
searchedFor: read src/lib/wafflebase-doc-store-cleanup.test.ts 'collection and live documents' and 'documents open in another tab'

samples.summary: The documented "local cleanup can never fail the deletion" property is never exercised — no test makes the purge reject
samples.evidence: `deleteDocument` awaits `purgeOfflineDocuments([id])` with the comment "Best effort, and never able to turn an accepted deletion into a reported failure", and `deleteWorkspace`/`removeMember` carry the same claim ("Local cleanup must never be able to fail the operation itself"). In `documents.test.ts` and `workspaces.test.ts` the purge is mocked and only ever resolves (`mockPurge.mockResolvedValue(undefined)`); the only failure injected is a rejecting *listing* (`mockDocuments.mockRejectedValue`). There is no `await` guard in the callers, so the property rests entirely on `purgeOfflineDocuments`'s internal try/catch — which no caller-level test pins.

samples.summary: The group-descendant case asserts an identity mapping, so it would also pass for an implementation that mapped the handle to itself rather than to the child's real id
samples.evidence: `mapDescendants` records `realIds.set(handle, child.id)` where `handle` is `child.__id ?? child.id`; the fixture gives the child only an `id`, so the expected value `"child-1"` is the same string as the key. `expect(connector.start.elementId).toBe('child-1')` therefore cannot distinguish a correct mapping from `realIds.set(handle, handle)`. The case still earns its keep (without `mapDescendants` the connector is dropped, and `droppedConnectors === 0` catches that), but adding a child with both `__id: 'tmp'` and `id: 'child-1'` would make the value itself load-bearing.

samples.summary: The "is the route saying so, not the default" control renders the mocked CollabDocumentProvider, so it asserts the context default rather than the real component
samples.evidence: The suite mocks `@/components/collab-document-provider` (line 24) to a probe, then at line 85 renders `<CollabDocumentProvider docKey="sheet-7" />` — the mock — and asserts `'true'`. That establishes only that `useDurabilityPermitted()` defaults to true outside a `NonDurableScope`, which is a one-line fact about `createContext(true)`. It does serve its stated purpose (the share-route probe reads `false` for a reason), so this is presentation rather than a coverage hole.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: offline-runtime.test.tsx captures the WafflebaseDocStore constructor options into `constructed` (line 37) but never asserts on them — `constructed` occurs only at lines 32, 37 and 96, and I read the entire file. The store class is fully mocked (lines 34-42), so nothing in the suite exercises or pins the `userId` passed at offline-runtime.tsx:77-80. Nearby assertions cover different consumers of the prop (`rememberOfflineUser` line 116, watcher getter `userOf()` line 135) and cannot fail if only the store construction used a wrong/stale identity; the recovery test asserts merely `expect(store).toBeDefined()` (line 271) and the purge test only `typeof options.isOpenElsewhere === 'function'` (line 168). I searched wide for a counterexample: OfflineRuntime is rendered nowhere else (grep across repo), private-route.test.tsx:73 asserts only the prop given to a mocked OfflineRuntime, packages/frontend/tests contains no offline-runtime coverage, and the wafflebase-doc-store*.test.ts files construct the store directly so they cannot pin the runtime's identity. Impact is real: wafflebase-doc-store.ts:983/1028/1052 scope listArchives/loadArchive strictly on this.userId, so a wrong construction identity would silently offer another account's archives for materialisation — a guard that could ship broken with this suite green. Over-mocking + missing assertion, in-lane and blocking.

finding.summary: The durability-lapse tooltip requirement is covered only by direct calls to the pure `tooltipFor`; nothing tests that a lapse published through context actually reaches the chip — and the provider nesting silently discards the durable client's reasons.
finding.evidence: `tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx` ("the tooltip on a state that is now designed rather than inevitable") calls `tooltipFor('not-saved', null, false, false, lapse)` directly with a hand-supplied lapse, so it passes regardless of whether `useDurabilityLapse()` ever answers anything. No test in the diff renders `SyncStatusChip` (or any consumer) beneath a `DurabilityLapseScope`: `durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx` has only a `Probe` for `useDocumentDurability()`, never `useDurabilityLapse()`, and `collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx` asserts nothing about lapse. That gap hides a live defect: `durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:220` wraps `children` in `DurabilityLapseScope lapse={lapse}`, and those children are `CollabDocumentProvider`'s `inner`, which at `collab-document-provider.tsx:302` mounts its *own* `DurabilityLapseScope` with `lapse === undefined` whenever `decided.durable` is true. The inner provider shadows the outer, so `dropped`, `too-large`, `out-of-space` and `write-failed` can never be read by anything under the document provider — exactly the opposite of the comment at durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:196 ("this wins where it has an answer"). The design requirement the tests cite ("its tooltip must name which case applies") therefore reads as covered while being unreachable in the app.

verdict.reason: The claimed-missing test exists. sync-status-chip.test.tsx:708-772 ('the lapse reaching the chip') renders a real <SyncStatusChip /> beneath two nested <DurabilityLapseScope>s in the app's order (helper at :710-734), opens the tooltip via fireEvent.focus and reads document.body.textContent — exercising useDurabilityLapse() through context rather than calling tooltipFor directly. It asserts a call-site-only cause reaches the chip (:736-738), a durable-client-only cause 'dropped' reaches it (:740-747), the client overrules the call site with 'out-of-space' while 'another-tab' is absent (:749-753), and that no scope at all degrades to pre-offline wording (:755-771). The reviewer's secondary premise is also false: collab-document-provider.tsx:301-311 shows `inner` contains no lapse scope, and the sole DurabilityLapseScope at :350-373 wraps BOTH branches from outside, so DurableYorkieProvider's scope (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:220) is the deeper winner as documented at :195-198. Additionally durable-document-context.ts:133-138 resolves `value: lapse ?? inherited`, so an undefined inner scope inherits rather than shadowing, making the alleged unreachability impossible in either nesting order.
